base: 16:9 landscape scene in Dadi's aangan in Gulmohar Mohalla on a calm late-October Sunday morning: a mud house with a clay-tile roof and a BROWN wooden door, a clean swept courtyard, a tulsi pot and a pot of orange marigolds, a big green gulmohar tree WITHOUT flowers, green fields behind; warm golden sun from one side, soft lavender shadows, light dust in the air. A pretend children's court is set up in the courtyard: a charpai at the back centre (the judge's seat), a small wooden patla next to it, a low bamboo-stick enclosure tied with string around one low wooden stool (mudha) on the RIGHT (the dock), a low wooden bench on the LEFT for waiting elders, a steel plate of round laddoos. Everyone wears their usual everyday clothes, no costumes. Family-friendly; the children look innocent and age-appropriate and are polite to the elders. No text, letters, words or numbers anywhere in the image (the notebook pages are blank).

scenes.prompt: Early morning setup of the pretend court, the courtyard still half-arranged: {golu} drags a charpai across the courtyard with both hands, excited, his back turned towards the parrot; {tinku} carries a steel plate of round laddoos carefully; {tara} places a wooden rolling pin (belan) on a small wooden patla, cheerful. On the left near the tulsi pot stands a simple wooden perch stand: {mitthu} sits on it with his beak open, calling, next to a small EMPTY, dry steel water bowl fixed to the perch (clearly visible, nothing inside). No adults in this image.

The pretend court is ready: {tara} sits cross-legged on the charpai at the back centre holding a wooden rolling pin like a judge's gavel, calm confident face, one finger raised as if stating a rule; {golu} stands proudly in front of the charpai like a lawyer, chest out; {tinku} stands beside the steel plate of laddoos holding a thin notebook with blank pages, proud; {mitthu} perches on the charpai's wooden rail. The bamboo dock on the right and the bench on the left are empty. No adults, no water bowl.

Arrival at the brown wooden door of the courtyard: {pandey} strides in smiling bossily, twirling his moustache with one hand, a lathi under his arm; {sharma} follows just behind him looking around worried as if searching for something, his rectangular spectacles pushed UP on his forehead; {golu}, {tara} and {tinku} stand in front greeting them politely with folded hands (namaste), smiling. The elders look happy to have been invited. No grandmother in this image.

Wide view of the pretend court in session: {pandey} sits on the low stool inside the bamboo dock on the RIGHT, amused, arms folded; on the low bench on the LEFT {sharma} (spectacles pushed up on his forehead) and {dadi} wait and smile; {tara} sits on the charpai at the back centre with the rolling pin; {tinku} stands announcing loudly, holding his blank notebook; {golu} walks like a lawyer in the middle, one hand raised; {mitthu} perches on the charpai's rail. Everyone is smiling; it is a happy game.

The 'evidence' moment in the pretend court: {tinku} holds up a broken round laddoo with a funny sad face; {mitthu} flaps his wings on the charpai rail with his beak wide open; {pandey} sits in the bamboo dock on the right with his chest puffed out, then a little sheepish half-smile under his moustache; {golu} points at the broken laddoo like a lawyer. Light and comic, nobody is upset.

The first verdict: on the LEFT third of the frame {tara} sits on the charpai and raises the wooden rolling pin high above the small wooden patla, a serious-but-kind judge face (clear, uncluttered space around her); on the right {pandey} sits in the bamboo dock whispering with one finger on his lips, eyes twinkling with fun; in the middle {golu} and {tinku} giggle behind their hands. Warm, playful, respectful.

The second case: {sharma} sits on the stool in the bamboo dock on the right looking around anxiously, his rectangular spectacles pushed UP on his forehead (no focus on his head, only the spectacles); {tinku} laughs kindly and taps his OWN forehead to show where the spectacles are; {golu} presents with an open palm like a lawyer; {tara} smiles on the charpai at the back; {mitthu} perches on the charpai rail.

The second verdict, a happy gift: {sharma} now wears his spectacles on his eyes, with a bright colourful braided cord tied to them hanging around his neck, laughing happily; {tara} stands beside the charpai having just given it to him, smiling; {golu} and {tinku} clap. Sharma ji looks delighted, not embarrassed.

The third case: {dadi} sits on the low stool inside the bamboo dock on the right, her walking stick beside her, one hand on her cheek in playful mock surprise, eyes laughing; {golu} presents with both hands spread wide as if saying 'so many stories'; {tara} sits on the charpai at the back smiling with the rolling pin; {tinku} stands with his blank notebook; {mitthu} perches on the charpai rail. The children are fond and respectful; Dadi enjoys the game.

The parrot's call: on the left near the tulsi pot {mitthu} sits on his wooden perch stand flapping his wings with his beak wide open, next to his EMPTY, dry steel water bowl (clearly visible, nothing inside); in the middle {golu} waves his hand dismissively without looking at the parrot, busy; {tinku} looks up from his blank notebook; {tara} has stood up from the charpai and looks straight at the dry bowl with a calm, focused thinking face. No adults in this image.

Close view: in the foreground the EMPTY dry steel water bowl on the wooden perch stand, {mitthu} on the perch looking down into it; in the soft background {tara}, {tinku} and {dadi} turn to look at {golu}; {golu} stands with a sorry, guilty face, hand behind his head. Gentle and caring mood, nobody is angry. No other adults.

{golu} kneels by the wooden perch stand and pours clean water from a small brass lota into the steel bowl; {mitthu} happily drinks from the bowl; {tara} and {tinku} stand beside smiling warmly. Soft morning sun, a tender moment.

Finale, wide: the whole group stands together in the LEFT 55% of the frame: {golu} stands straight in front of the charpai with a hand on his heart; {tara} on the charpai holds the rolling pin with a kind smile; {tinku} holds the plate of laddoos happily; {pandey} laughs with a hand over his mouth; {sharma} (colourful cord on his spectacles, spectacles on his eyes) and {dadi} smile on the bench; {mitthu} sits on his perch with the steel bowl now full of water. The RIGHT side of the frame is calm and empty of people: the brown door, the marigold pot, the green fields in soft sunlight.
